title: Interfacial Structure in GaAs/Al0.55Ga0.45As Asymmetric Coupled Quantum Wells Revealed by Advanced Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy
content: Semiconductor multi-quantum wells (MQWs) provide an ideal playground for researchers in the nanoscale domain to innovate and develop new device architectures, leveraging the foundational principles of quantum mechanics to enhance second order non-linearities. Over the past few decades, the utilization of such MQW structures has seen a continuous expansion in various optoelectronic applications including lasers, photodetectors, optical modulators and solar cells. The concept of leveraging asymmetric coupled quantum wells (ACQWs), pioneered by Khurgin [1], promises enhanced second-order non-linear susceptibility (χ2) through symmetry breaking. Yet, enhancement in χ2 values from ACQWs relies on precise quantum confinement, highlighting the need for meticulous control over the sharpness of interfaces [2]. Employing atomic-scale scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and multi-slice ptychography [3,4], we identify the three-dimensional interfacial structures in GaAs/AlGaAs ACQWs, aiming to elucidate the influence of interfaces on χ2.
